newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees spate of new orders.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees spate of new orders.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a wealth of fresh inquiry at the start of the week but few fixtures were reported, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Cargill quoted for 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Punta Morales to US Gulf/Atlantic for February 1/10 and 12/14,000 tonnes bulk/bagged from Thailand to South Korea or Indonesia for 1/5 February.
Glencore was open for 13/14,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to east Africa for prompt/12 February dates.
Czarnikow Rionda was in the market for a prompt 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar form Puerto Quetzal to west Africa.

Kerry Foodstuffs was open for tonnage for two Asian orders, 14,000 tonnes bulk from Thailand to South Korea and prompt/onwards and 11,000 tonnes from India to Indonesia, with the possibility of increasing to 13,000 tonnes.

Bruce quoted three account orders for bagged suagr -- 14/14,300 tonnes from Thailand to Indonesia for 29 January/3 February, 3/4,000 from Antwerp to Haifa/Ashdod for the start of February and 1,000 from Odessa to Poti for 3/7 February.
It was also open for 13,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Cuba to Syria for prompt dates.
Man was active at the start of week, quoting a number of new orders and repeating some from last week, shipbrokers said.
It was open for 14,000 tonnes from Coatzacoalcos or Veracruz to Colombo for prompt/seven days and 12/14,000 tones min/max bagged sugar from Madras to east Africa with Red Sea option.
Man was also in the market for 12,500 tonnes min/max from Thailand to Indonesia for 1/15 February and 12/16,000 tonnes from Acajutla to Djibouti option Colombo for 27 January/10 February.
Other orders were for 23/25,000 tonnes in bulk from Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for 25 January/5 February and 1,200/1,700 tonnes in bags from Bourgas to Poti for 27/30 January.
Allen Chartering cited an account order for 5,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Antwerp to Oran for end-January to the start of February.
Shyvers Savoy quoted for tonnage on account to ship 4,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rouen/Antwerp range to Nouakchott for 20/25 February.

The six-day-old strike in the Colombian port of Buenaventura is said to have paralysed the export of at least 27,000 tonnes of sugar, of which 17,000 tonnes was bulk in containers and another 10,000 tonnes in 200,000 50-kg sacks.
Six ships are currently moored at quayside with another six anchored and waiting to dock.
Since the start of the industrial action, at least 12 vessels have been diverted to Colombia's Caribbean coastal ports via Balboa in Panama or have docked in Guayaquil, Ecuador.
